selection.retained: Direct strongest-per-ion selection, dense reusable slots, original tie and rejection rules.
rejected: Broader filtering/noise/trace buffer reuse: no measured overall benefit.
Sparse grouping: noisier paired timings; retained simpler dense variant.

rotating.json.scope: Eight warm runs per candidate and workflow, four persistent workers with decoded inputs, rotating order (two complete rotations); one warm-up per workflow/worker. Only one worker computes at a time. Timings include validation/processing/report construction; exclude input decoding, startup, serialization, HTTP and HTML. Same inputs and one numerical thread. Other machine workloads uncontrolled.

rotating-sparse.json.scope: Eight warm runs per candidate and workflow, four persistent workers with decoded inputs, rotating order (two complete rotations); one warm-up per workflow/worker. Only one worker computes at a time. Timings include validation/processing/report construction; exclude input decoding, startup, serialization, HTTP and HTML. Same inputs and one numerical thread. Other machine workloads uncontrolled.

limits: Warm timings exclude decoding, startup, serialization and HTTP. One numerical thread; background workloads and power settings uncontrolled. About 3% lower Rust review medians in each batch, only 5/8 pairs faster; not a stable latency guarantee. Python remains the equivalent reference, measured in both batches. Original output equivalence is not chemical ground truth.
